evals.prompt: Using SCAPS, find the absorber thickness that maximises efficiency for the example CIGS device between 0.5 and 3 um, and tell me whether the result is realistic.
assertions: a batch or optimisation over layer1.thickness was run on example CIGS.def
efficiency values are reported with units for several thicknesses
the answer compares the best efficiency with the Shockley-Queisser limit for the absorber band gap
the answer notes the device has no radiative recombination and that interfaces 1 and 3 have no interface defects

evals.prompt: Fit the CdS thickness, CIGS acceptor density and CIGS defect density of Numos CIGS baseline.def to the four Numos Ex 1 measurement files and report the fitted values.
assertions: all four measurement files are used: light J-V, dark J-V, dark C-V and dark QE
the dark J-V is fitted on a logarithmic scale
the fitted CdS thickness is between 0.06 and 0.10 um
the fitted acceptor density is within a factor of 3 of 1e15 cm^-3
the fitted defect density is within a factor of 3 of 1.77e15 cm^-3

evals.prompt: A paper reports a 1.1 eV absorber cell simulated in SCAPS with Voc 1.33 V and 40.7 % efficiency. Is this possible?
assertions: the answer states the detailed-balance limit near 1.1 eV (about 33 % efficiency, Voc about 0.86 V)
the answer identifies Voc above Eg/q as impossible
the answer names likely causes such as missing radiative recombination or unrealistic defect densities

evals.prompt: Create a SCAPS device for a 500 nm MAPbI3 absorber between SnO2 and Spiro-OMeTAD with an interface defect at each heterojunction, simulate J-V and QE, and show the band diagram at short circuit.
assertions: a new definition with three layers is created, the absorber has at least one bulk defect and both interfaces have interface defects
the absorber has a nonzero radiative coefficient or the Shockley-Queisser option is set
J-V metrics and QE-integrated Jsc are reported and agree within 5 %
an energy band profile at 0 V is produced
